results.title: Binance Agent OS: AI Agents Can Now Trade Crypto
results.content:
Binance’s Agentic Wallet imposes more explicit limits on some activities. Reported default limits include up to $50,000 per day for regular swaps, $100,000 per day for DeFi transactions, and $20 per day for x402 payments.

Those limits should not be confused with exchange-trading limits inside Agent OS subaccounts.

The system is therefore less like handing an AI agent a normal Binance login and more like constructing a financial sandbox around it.

How safe that sandbox is depends partly on how the user configures it.

The Competitive Landscape

Binance is not alone in opening its infrastructure to AI agents. The move follows a wave of similar initiatives from rival exchanges over the past several months. Agents operate within dedicated subaccounts with withdrawals blocked by default, creating a sandbox around their activity. Agent OS extends beyond order placement. This positions agents not just as trading bots but as potential on-chain operators capable of managing funds across strategies, executing routine transactions, and coordinating multi-step workflows.
